## New features
- **Edit a road's nodes and segments directly in the plan.** Selecting a road now shows just its centre nodes. Double-click a node or a segment to edit it: its width handles appear with the width written across the road, and a small bar beside it offers width, height and, for a segment, a Bridge switch. Drag one end of a segment to change that end, or hold Shift to keep both ends equal (Alt gives 1 cm steps). Alt-click adds or removes a node, Delete removes the selected node and Esc finishes. The same actions are on the road's right-click menu.
- **Set road heights the way you think about them.** Raise or lower a node or segment relative to its normal height (the default when the project has terrain), as a height above the ground, or as an absolute level. Raised or lowered road still builds an embankment or cutting that follows it.
- **Bridges per segment.** Switch Bridge on for just the segment that crosses another road or a valley. A bridge segment runs straight between its nodes and leaves the ground below untouched. If a bridge deck would pass below the ground between its nodes, the Inspector says so.

## Changes
- **A clearer road Inspector.** One overall width sits next to the road type; dual carriageways and motorways add both carriageway widths and the reservation on one row. Fields sit two or three to a row when the panel is wide enough, the section for the selected node or segment opens by itself, and the detailed per-node table, carriageway geometry, calibration and project settings stay folded away until needed. Choosing a road type now applies its widths to the whole road.
- **Full screen uses the standard macOS title bar**, dark in Dark Mode, and the extra space around the menus eases in instead of jumping.
- **Updates install inside AURIS** even when it was started from source, into the copy in Applications.

## Bug fixes
- **A road marked as a bridge no longer runs inside a hill.** A bridge running end to end along a hillside road sat up to 5 m below the ground; a bridge now never dips below the ground at its interior nodes.
- **Dragging a dual carriageway's width no longer turns it into a single carriageway.** Each node keeps at least two 3 m carriageways plus the reservation.
- **CRTN emission with ISO 9613-2 propagation keeps both carriageways of a dual road whose width varies.** It had combined them into one centre line; full CRTN was not affected.
- **The red source lines follow the true kerbs** in the plan and 3D where a road's width varies.
- **Single-track roads have no centre line**, and the central barrier of a dual carriageway is galvanised steel in 3D rather than black.
